purpose: Teach: 属する/従う/密接/超過/所在/着手/急増/取り上げる

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、学界に、本気で、絶対、属する、絶対、研究者として、絶対、責任、絶対、果たせ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Ren — I need you to commit yourself fully to the academic world. As a researcher, carry that responsibility with absolute seriousness.
lines.style: Measured, deliberate. Opens with Ren's name — direct attention. Each clause lands with quiet weight. Pauses between phrases like punctuation marks. Not loud, but unmissable. The tone of someone who has seen many researchers falter and means to ensure this one won't.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。教授の指導に、本気で、絶対、従う、絶対、進めております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm following your guidance with full commitment, and I'm advancing with genuine gratitude for your direction.
lines.style: Formal but sincere — not stiff. Slight bow in the voice. Steady eye contact through the words. Respectful without being effusive. The careful registration of a student who understands the weight of what was just asked.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 教授と、本気で、絶対、密接、絶対、な、絶対、議論、絶対、続けろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Keep maintaining close, rigorous discussion with your advisor. That's non-negotiable.
lines.style: Firm, instructive. Slight lean forward in the phrasing. 'Close' and 'rigorous' both receive small emphasis — not sharp, but clear. The delivery of someone who knows exactly what breaks researchers: isolation. No room for negotiation here.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。研究時間、本気で、絶対、超過、絶対、しないよう、絶対、管理しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm managing my research hours carefully so I don't exceed my limits, and I'm grateful for your oversight.
lines.style: Earnest, grounded. Voice settles into a rhythm of responsibility — not defensive, but present. Slight emphasis on 'managing' and 'carefully.' The tone of someone taking the advice seriously, not just hearing it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 研究、本気で、絶対、所在、絶対、明らかに、絶対、しろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Make your research direction clear and transparent. Don't let it become diffuse.
lines.style: Sharp but not unkind. The words land like someone setting stakes. Slight hardening on 'clear' and 'transparent.' Delivered with the weariness of someone who has watched too many brilliant students scatter their focus. A teacher correcting, not scolding.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。新規論文に、本気で、絶対、着手、絶対、いたしました、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I've already begun work on a new paper, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to demonstrate that focus.
lines.style: Prompt, almost eager to show compliance. Voice has a hint of relief — the student has understood and is already moving. 'Begun' lands with small pride. Sincere gratitude, not performative. The tone of someone who heard the unspoken warning and acted.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 論文発表の、本気で、絶対、急増、絶対、注視しろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Watch the surge in paper publications closely. Don't miss the trends in your field.
lines.style: Urgent but controlled. 'Watch' opens with slight intensity. 'Surge' receives a small emphasis — something is happening, pay attention. Steady pace, no fluster. The instruction of a senior who sees something moving in the academic landscape that matters.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。海外論文も、本気で、絶対、取り上げる、絶対、姿勢、絶対、続けてまいります、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm continuing to engage with international papers and staying attuned to global scholarship, with sincere appreciation for your guidance.
lines.style: Determined, closing note. Voice settles into committed rhythm. 'International' and 'global' both carry slight emphasis — the student has understood the scope. Trailing slightly softer on the gratitude, like a respectful bow. The tone of someone who has heard the full message and means to act on it.
